questions.title: Organization structure/chart of the government
questions.text: Organization structure/chart of the government — A diagrammatic representation of the structure of a government organization or agency. It illustrates the hierarchy, relationships, roles, and respons
questions.what: A diagrammatic representation of the structure of a government organization or agency. It illustrates the hierarchy, relationships, roles, and responsibilities of various departments, units, and positions within the government.
questions.why: A government organogram promotes transparency, accountability, eﬃcient communication, citizen engagement, service access, and even legal and regulatory compliance in some cases.

how.scoring_guidance: 1. Visual Representation: a. Create a clear and concise diagram outlining the national organization's structure. 2. Accessibility and Transparency: a. Publish the diagram prominently on the national portal for easy public access. b. Ensure the diagram is in a widely compatible format (e.g., PDF or PNG) for easy viewing. 3. Detailed Descriptions: a. Provide brief descriptions of each department or unit represented in the diagram. b. Include contact information, key responsibilities, and services oﬀered by each department. 4. Regular Updates: a. Reﬂect any changes in staﬃng, departments, or reporting lines promptly to maintain accuracy.

questions.title: Names and titles of heads of department
questions.text: Names and titles of heads of department — A section, chart or webpage displaying the names, oﬃcial titles, and contact information (such as phone numbers and email addresses) of individuals le
questions.what: A section, chart or webpage displaying the names, oﬃcial titles, and contact information (such as phone numbers and email addresses) of individuals leading various government departments or ministries.
questions.why: This information allows individuals, businesses, or other stakeholders to directly communicate with the heads of these departments regarding speciﬁc matters, services, or concerns. It also promotes transparency, accountability, and accessibility.

Commit to keeping the information up-to-date, reﬂecting any changes in department leadership.

questions.title: Links to sub-national/local government institutions/agencies

questions.what: A dedicated section of relative hyperlinks to subnational/local government agencies' oﬃcial websites.
questions.why: These links serve as direct access points, allowing residents to quickly ﬁnd speciﬁc agency information, services, and resources.

questions.title: Privacy statement(s)
questions.text: Privacy statement(s) — A formal statement, often found in the footer or home page either explicitly stated or in a related link, explains how the website collects, processes
questions.what: A formal statement, often found in the footer or home page either explicitly stated or in a related link, explains how the website collects, processes, stores, & protects the personal information of its users.
questions.why: Essential for establishing trust with users, ensuring compliance with relevant privacy laws and regulations, and demonstrating the government’s commitment to protecting people’s privacy

how.scoring_guidance: 1. Clear Language: a. Write the policy in simple, understandable language. b. Specify what user information is collected & detail methods: cookies, forms, or third-party. 3. questions.title: National e-Government/Digital Government Strategy
questions.text: National e-Government/Digital Government Strategy — The National e-Government or Digital Government Strategy is a comprehensive plan devised by national governments to leverage digital technologies for
questions.what: The National e-Government or Digital Government Strategy is a comprehensive plan devised by national governments to leverage digital technologies for improving public services and governance. It should be readily accessible and openly available to the public on the government's website.
questions.why: A National e-Government/Digital Government Strategy ensures eﬃcient and transparent delivery of public services through the strategic use of digital technologies.

how.scoring_guidance: Indicative Steps 1. Assess Digital Infrastructure: a. Evaluate existing digital systems and infrastructure for gaps and strengths. 2. Engage Stakeholders: a. Involve relevant stakeholders from various sectors to gather insights and ensure inclusivity. 3. Set Clear Objectives: a. Deﬁne speciﬁc, measurable goals aligned with national priorities and public service needs. 4. Publish Strategy Online: a. Make the strategy accessible to the public via the government's website for transparency and accountability. 5. Monitor and Adapt: a. Establish mechanisms for continuous monitoring, evaluation, and adaptation to evolving technological and societal trends.

questions.why: The right to access information enables all individuals to know how the decisions that aﬀect them are made, how public funds are handled and according to which criteria institutions act.

questions.why: Crucial for ensuring transparency, compliance, and public awareness regarding measures taken to protect digital assets and people’s online safety.

how.scoring_guidance: 1. Research and Consultation: a. Conduct thorough research and consult with stakeholders to understand cybersecurity needs and gather input. 2. Draft Legislation: a. questions.title: Establishment:
questions.text: Establishment: — Name of the national Chief Information Oﬃcer (CIO) or equivalent who oversees and directs the implementation of digital government strategies and prog
questions.what: Name of the national Chief Information Oﬃcer (CIO) or equivalent who oversees and directs the implementation of digital government strategies and programs at the national level, ensuring eﬃcient and eﬀective use of technology to enhance public services and governance.
questions.why: Ensures transparency and clarity about the leadership responsible for driving digital transformation and e-government initiatives.

how.scoring_guidance: 1. Establishment: a. Set up a dedicated oﬃce speciﬁcally for the national Chief Information Oﬃcer (CIO). 2. Responsibilities and Authority: a. Clearly deﬁne the responsibilities and authority of the CIO in spearheading e-government strategies and programs. 3. Recruitment: a. Recruit an individual with a strong background in information technology and public administration to eﬀectively fulﬁll the CIO role. 4. Collaboration: a. Ensure seamless collaboration and coordination between the CIO oﬃce and relevant government agencies to streamline e-government initiatives. 5. Regular Review: a. Implement a system for regular review and update of the CIO's mandate.
